sourceRefs.locator: Chapter 7, pp. 102–108, Figs. 7.2–4 and Table 7.1. Hearth 4A76P west of the brook, 15 grey-green chert flakes one metre west of the fire, the nail one metre southeast. With 1950 as BP reference, the reported two-sigma charcoal ranges are AD 900–910 and 960–1040 for Beta-252632 and AD 990–1150 for Beta-252633. The map uses their outer envelope; occupation was episodic. pp. 115–116 and Tables 7.5–6 describe birds on the other, upper terrace.

Arctic Anthropology 49(1), pp. 68–87, DOI 10.1353/arc.2012.0015. Abstract and Table 1 discuss the site in relation to Beothuk ancestors, the charcoal determinations for hearth 4A76P2 and seasonal harvesting of birds.
First two paragraphs. Archaeological evidence of Indigenous use over six millennia and Dorset camps on the south shore more than two centuries before the Norse.
